title: Cover — Investment Proposal
description: Title slide: IQRA wordmark, positioning line, seed round 2026, confidential.
speakerNotes:
Open calmly and with conviction. Let the title sit for a beat before you speak.

- "IQRA is authenticated Islamic knowledge, built for the age of generative AI."
- "We're a live product, not a concept. Today I'll show you the problem, what we've built, the market, and a specific ask."
- Set the frame: this is a seed round, and everything I share is confidential.

Keep it to ~20 seconds. Do not read the whole slide — say the one line and move.

title: Executive Summary
description: The whole argument in five lines: problem, solution, market, model, ask.
speakerNotes:
This is the whole pitch in five lines. If someone had to leave after one slide, this is the slide.

- General AI answers faith questions probabilistically — it produces rulings no one can verify.
- IQRA anchors every answer in authenticated sources and a verified chain of transmission, the Isnad.
- The market is enormous: two billion Muslims and a $2.4 trillion Islamic economy.
- The model scales in three steps — donations today, premium tooling next, B2B licensing after.
- The ask: $2.5M to reach one million daily users and B2B revenue within 24 months.

Deliver these as five clean statements, then say: "Let me take each of these in turn."

title: Problem
description: Generative AI manufactures unverifiable religious rulings; doctrinal drift at scale.
speakerNotes:
Name the problem plainly. This is a trust problem, not a technology problem.

- Large language models predict plausible text. They are not built to verify a ruling.
- That produces doctrinal drift: fabricated citations, blended traditions, confident errors — at scale.
- Two billion Muslims are already asking these questions online, and a wrong answer here carries real spiritual weight.
- No mainstream assistant grounds its guidance in an authenticated chain of transmission.

Pause after the spiritual-weight line — it is the emotional center of the pitch. Cite Pew for the population figure.

title: Solution
description: Retrieval-grounded assistant, five domains, Isnad Board governance, built-in guardrails.
speakerNotes:
Now the answer. Emphasize that authenticity is architectural, not cosmetic.

- IQRA is retrieval-grounded: every answer ties back to classical texts, not model guesswork.
- It covers five domains — creed, jurisprudence of transactions, hadith authentication, ethics, and history.
- An Isnad Board of verified scholars governs what enters the knowledge base — no synthetic or plagiarized content.
- Guardrails are built in: a Zero Comparative Religion policy and a total ban on optimizing Haram activity.
- Every answer is tagged with its scriptural anchor, so users can verify the source themselves.

Land the point: "The chain of transmission is the moat. Anyone can build a chatbot; almost no one can build the governance."

title: Traction
description: Honest built/status table: live app, ingested KB, active Q&A, operational admin.
speakerNotes:
This is the credibility slide. Be precise and honest — no user-count claims.

- The product is live at iqra.live: a web app and installable PWA, secure accounts, multi-thread chat.
- The knowledge base holds 400+ classical source documents — about 58,000 searchable passages — already ingested.
- 500 curated scholar-style Q&A pairs are actively guiding answer quality.
- Donations, admin knowledge management, and analytics are operational.

Say it directly: "We are not pitching a slide deck. We are pitching a system that already works. The capital is to scale it, not to build it."

title: Market
description: Population and Islamic economy sizing with sources; near-term online wedge.
speakerNotes:
Size the opportunity with real numbers, then narrow to the wedge.

- Two billion Muslims in 2025, rising to 2.2 billion by 2030 — growing about twice the global rate.
- Muslim consumer spending across core sectors: $2.43 trillion in 2023, heading to $3.36 trillion by 2028.
- Islamic finance assets: from $4.9 trillion to $7.5 trillion over the same window.
- The near-term wedge is the billion-plus Muslims already online and underserved by authentic tools.

Attribute the figures: Pew, DinarStandard's State of the Global Islamic Economy, and Standard Chartered. Then: "We don't need the whole market — just the online, underserved edge of it."

title: Business Model
description: Three phases: philanthropy, premium tooling, B2B licensing.
speakerNotes:
Walk the three phases as a sequence, not three bets at once.

- Phase 1, today: in-app donations fund operations. It aligns with the mission and proves willingness to pay.
- Phase 2: premium tooling — Zakat calculator, Halal investment checklist, estate planning, corporate Zakat audits.
- Phase 3, Year 2 and beyond: B2B licensing — API access and compliance chatbots for Halal marketplaces and institutions.
- Unit economics improve as we go: cost per query is targeted to fall about 40% over 12 months as knowledge confidence rises.

Be clear the 40% is a management target, not a result yet. Frame B2B as the high-margin endgame.

title: Growth
description: Three growth engines: community, product depth, partnerships; milestone path.
speakerNotes:
Explain how we get to a million daily users — three engines working together.

- Community: mosque, university, and scholar networks. Source-cited answers are inherently shareable.
- Product depth: premium tools convert engaged users, and the PWA install removes friction.
- Partnerships: Islamic institutions and libraries give us both credibility and distribution.
- The path: live product, to an engaged base, to one million daily users — the funded 24-month goal.

Say explicitly that the million is a target, not a current number. Credibility depends on that honesty.

title: Expansion
description: Expansion across knowledge, language, and market.
speakerNotes:
Show the roadmap on three axes so investors see durability.

- Knowledge: from 400+ documents toward 100,000 authenticated primary sources, through library partnerships. This is the deepening moat.
- Language: beyond English into Arabic, Urdu, and Bahasa — 60% of Muslims live in Asia-Pacific, so language is distribution.
- Market: consumer app first, then B2B API and compliance tooling for the Halal economy.

Tie it back: "Each axis compounds the others — more sources make better answers, more languages reach more users, and both make the B2B product more valuable."

title: The Ask
description: $2.5M seed for ~15% equity; use-of-funds breakdown and indicative terms.
speakerNotes:
Be direct and specific. Investors respect a clear number and a clear use of funds.

- We are raising $2.5M in seed capital.
- Allocation: 30% to Knowledge and the Isnad Board, 30% to engineering and AI infrastructure, 20% to product, 15% to growth and community, 5% held in reserve.
- Indicative terms: $2.5M for roughly 15% equity, about $16.7M post-money, via SAFE or a priced round.
- One condition on our side: values-aligned capital only. Partners uphold the Zero Comparative Religion policy and the Isnad Board's independence.

Deliver the number without hedging. The values condition is a strength — it signals discipline, not naivety.

title: Justification
description: Why $2.5M and why now: runway, defensibility, unit economics, B2B, right-sizing.
speakerNotes:
Answer the two questions every investor is holding: why this amount, and why now.

- $2.5M buys about 24 months of runway — enough to hit the milestones you'd underwrite.
- It funds the jump from 400+ to 100,000 authenticated sources, which is the core defensibility.
- It targets the ~40% reduction in cost per query as knowledge confidence rises.
- It stands up the B2B API alpha — the door to high-margin recurring revenue in Year 2 and beyond.
- And it's right-sized: enough to reach scale and B2B, small enough to keep the round efficient and founder-aligned.

Close this slide with: "This is the smallest amount that still gets us to a fundable Series A."

title: Closing
description: Closing lockup: mission line, positioning, contact details.
speakerNotes:
Return to the mission. End on conviction, not logistics.

- "IQRA is an investment in the integrity of Islamic knowledge."
- "We hold the defensible position in authenticated Islamic AI — a live product, a governed knowledge base, and a clear path to revenue."
- Give the contact and invite the next conversation: iqra.live, invest@iqra.live.

Stop talking after the mission line lands. Let the silence do the closing work, then open for questions.
